arxiv-2302-14395.title: Item Cold Start Recommendation via Adversarial Variational Autoencoder Warm-up
arxiv-2302-14395.creator: Shenzheng Zhang, Qi Tan, Xinzhi Zheng, Yi Ren, Xu Zhao, Wang Nian
arxiv-2302-14395.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Shenzheng Zhang, Qi Tan, Xinzhi Zheng, Yi Ren, Xu Zhao, Wang Nian. With numerous pieces of information emerging daily and greatly influencing people’s lives, large-scale recommendation systems are necessary for timely bridging the users with their desired information. However, the existing widely used embedding-based recommendation systems have a shortcoming in recommending new items because little interaction data is available for training new item ID embedding, which is recognized as item cold start problem.

arxiv-2303-17984.title: Models as Agents: Optimizing Multi-Step Predictions of Interactive Local Models in Model-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2303-17984.creator: Zifan Wu, Chao Yu, Chen Chen, Jianye Hao, Hankz Hankui Zhuo
arxiv-2303-17984.description: Abstract Research in model-based reinforcement learning has made significant progress in recent years. Compared to single-agent settings, the exponential dimension growth of the joint state-action space in multi-agent systems dramatically increases the complexity of the environment dynamics, which makes it infeasible to learn an accurate global model and thus necessitates the use of agent-wise local models.

arxiv-2304-01540.title: Gonosomal algebras and associated discrete-time dynamical systems
arxiv-2304-01540.creator: U.A. Rozikov, S.K. Shoyimardonov, R. Varro
arxiv-2304-01540.description: Abstract . In this paper we study the discrete-time dynamical systems associated with gonosomal algebras used as algebraic model in the sex-linked genes inheritance. We show that the class of gonosomal algebras is disjoint from the other non-associative algebras usually studied (Lie, alternative, Jordan, associative power).

arxiv-2402-19409.title: C 10 C_{10} has positive Turán density in the hypercube
arxiv-2402-19409.creator: Alexandr Grebennikov, João Pedro Marciano
arxiv-2402-19409.description: Abstract . The n n -dimensional hypercube Q n Q_{n} is a graph with vertex set { 0 , 1 } n \{0,1\}^{n} such that there is an edge between two vertices if and only if they differ in exactly one coordinate.

arxiv-2403-11141.title: The Simplex Projection: Lossless Visualization of 4D Compositional Data on a 2D Canvas
arxiv-2403-11141.creator: Marvin Schmitt, Yuga Hikida, Stefan T. Radev, Filip Sadlo, Paul-Christian Bürkner
arxiv-2403-11141.description: Abstract The simplex projection expands the capabilities of simplex plots (also known as ternary plots) to achieve a lossless visualization of 4D compositional data on a 2D canvas. Previously, this was only possible for 3D compositional data. We demonstrate how our approach can be applied to individual data points, point clouds, and continuous probability density functions on simplices.

arxiv-2411-18370.title: One-stop strategy to search for long-duration gravitational-wave signals
arxiv-2411-18370.creator: Rodrigo Tenorio, Joan-René Mérou, Alicia M. Sintes
arxiv-2411-18370.description: Abstract Blind continuous gravitational-wave (CWs) searches are a significant computational challenge due to their long duration and weak amplitude of the involved signals. To cope with such problem, the community has developed a variety of data-analysis strategies which are usually tailored to specific CW searches; this prevents their applicability across the nowadays broad landscape of potential CW source.

arxiv-2509-01428.title: Generalizations of Ferber-Krivelevich and Gallai Theorems on parity of degrees in induced subgraphs
arxiv-2509-01428.creator: Jiangdong Ai Qiwen Guo Gregory Gutin Yiming Hao Anders Yeo
arxiv-2509-01428.description: Abstract A long-standing and well-known conjecture (see e.g. Caro, Discrete Math, 1994) states that every n n -vertex graph G G without isolated vertices contains an induced subgraph where all vertices have an odd degree and whose order is linear in n n . Ferber and Krivelevich (Adv. Math., 2022) confirmed the conjecture.

arxiv-2511-07263.title: Alloy-Driven Verification of Object-Centric Event Data: From Temporal Logic to Knowledge Graphs
arxiv-2511-07263.creator: Saba Latif, Huma Latif, Touseef Ur Rehman, Muhammad Rameez Ur Rahman
arxiv-2511-07263.description: Abstract Object-centric process mining addresses the limitations of traditional approaches, which often involve the lossy flattening of event data and obscure vital relationships among interacting objects. This paper presents a novel formal framework for Object-centric Event Data (OCED) that ensures the correctness of the meta-model and preserves native object-centric semantics prior to the system implementation.

arxiv-2512-01851.title: Classical Reconstruction of the PMNS Matrix Using a Mechanical Neutrino Oscillator
arxiv-2512-01851.creator: Nishil Savla
arxiv-2512-01851.description: Abstract Neutrino oscillations arise from quantum interference between neutrino mass eigenstates and are governed by the PMNS matrix. Although this is an intrinsically quantum phenomenon, its mathematical structure is analogous to systems of coupled classical oscillators. In this work, a three–pendulum system connected by springs is constructed as a classical analog of three–flavor neutrino oscillations.

pmc-10630181.title: Predicting of Mechanical Ventilation and Outcomes by Using Models and Biomarker in Guillain-Barré Syndrome
pmc-10630181.creator: Jiajia Yao, Rumeng Zhou, Yue Liu, Yin Liu, Qian Cao, Zuneng Lu
pmc-10630181.description: BackgroundGuillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) is an acute inflammatory neuropathy. The Erasmus GBS Respiratory Insufficiency Score (EGRIS) and the modified Erasmus GBS Outcome Score (mEGOS) are prognostic models used in the prediction of mechanical ventilation and outcome. Thus far, there are only few biomarkers for the prognosis prediction of GBS patients, and albumin level is one that is promising.

pmc-11456818.title: Follow-up report on pulmonary mucosa-associated lymphoma in a patient with von Hippel–Lindau disease
pmc-11456818.creator: Bukola A Olarewaju, Judy B Tejon, Mayowa A Osundiji
pmc-11456818.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). With the increasing opportunities for medical management of von Hippel–Lindau (VHL)-related lesions, fundamental questions are arising regarding the possibilities of the FDA-approved medication (Belzutifan) to delay the progression of other non-VHL-related tumors that are not requiring urgent surgical interventions. We present a follow-up report on a VHL patient, with a co-morbid history of pulmonary mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma, who was initially described in the clinical scientific literature ~10 years ago.

pmc-11504069.title: Parental Phubbing Behavior and Adolescents’ Online Gaming Time: The Mediating Role of Electronic Health Literacy
pmc-11504069.creator: Jinnan Liu, Tao Xie, Ying Mao, Xiaochun Xie
pmc-11504069.description: Objective: The purpose of this study is to explore the relationship between parents’ phubbing behavior and children’s online gaming time. More importantly, we investigated the mediating role of electronic health literacy in this association. Methods: A total of 1200 questionnaires were sent out and 1130 effective questionnaires were returned, an effective recovery of 94.17%.

pmc-11666741.title: Arabidopsis VQ motif-containing proteins VQ1 and VQ10 interact with plastidial 1-deoxy-D-xylulose-5-phosphate synthase
pmc-11666741.creator: Beatriz Gayubas, Mari-Cruz Castillo, José León
pmc-11666741.description: VQ1 and VQ10 are largely unstructured homologous proteins with a significant potential for protein–protein interactions. Yeast two-hybrid (Y2H) analysis confirmed that both proteins interact not only with themselves and each other but also with other VQ and WRKY proteins. Screening an Arabidopsis Y2H library with VQ1 as bait identified 287 interacting proteins.

pmc-11691530.title: PATIENT PRIORITIES CARE (PPC) IN HISPANIC PATIENTS WITH DEMENTIA
pmc-11691530.creator: Alejandra Mera, Emily Peel, Aanand Naik, Rafael Samper-Ternent
pmc-11691530.description: Hispanics are the fastest growing underrepresented population in the U.S and have a higher risk of dementia compared to non-Hispanic whites. Lack of trust, limited health care access, and lack of culturally adapted interventions contribute to health disparities in this population group. Patient Priorities Care (PPC) is an evidenced-based approach that improves health outcomes in patients with multimorbidity.

pmc-11772336.title: Transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation for Parkinson’s disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-11772336.creator: Jiatong Shan, Zehong Li, Minxiu Ji, Miao Zhang, Caidi Zhang, Yikang Zhu, Zhen Feng
pmc-11772336.description: BackgroundTranscutaneous vagus nerve stimulation (tVNS) has emerged as a novel noninvasive adjunct therapy for advanced Parkinson’s disease (PD), yet no quantitative analysis had been conducted to assess its therapeutic effect.ObjectivesThis review aimed to investigate the efficacy of tVNS on motor function, other potential clinical targets and its safety in various treatment conditions.

pmc-12468544.title: Temporomandibular Disorders in Professional Scuba Divers—A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-12468544.creator: Ivica Pelivan, Joško Viskić, Nikša Dulčić, Maciej Chęciński
pmc-12468544.description: Objectives: Most of the published literature on this topic argues about painful teeth, masticatory muscles, and/or temporomandibular joints in scuba divers. This study aimed to determine the possible differences in the prevalence of TMD between the diver population and the general population. Methods: This was a cross-sectional epidemiological study.

pmc-12567739.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). In increasingly complex electromagnetic environments, wireless communication systems face the severe challenge of non-Gaussian impulse noise. The moments of impulse noise tend toward infinity, reducing the distinguishability of signal features and thereby limiting improvements in signal modulation recognition rates. First, a time–frequency analysis method based on kernel space mapping is proposed to improve the distinguishability of time–frequency features in signals under impulse noise.

Using RSM with a BBD, the combined impact of aw (0.92–0.99), pH (5.6–6.

pmc-12827471.title: Doping-induced magnetic phase transition enables all-electrical spin control in CrSBr
pmc-12827471.creator: Guorui Zhao, Yibin Zhao, Yu Zhang, Kunlin Yang, Zejing Guo, Jiaqi Liu, Tuoyu Zhao, Kun Yan, Xiaobin Chen, Qi Li, Yingchun Cheng, Cheng Zhang, Zhe Wang, Yi Liu, Jianting Ye, Jia-Wei Mei, Zhe Yuan, Wu Shi
pmc-12827471.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Van der Waals antiferromagnetic semiconductors are promising platforms for energy-efficient two-dimensional spintronics. However, their intrinsic spin degeneracy and the difficulty of achieving electrical spin control pose major challenges for practical device implementation. Here, we present a distinct spintronic platform based on an antiferromagnetic semiconductor CrSBr, in which carrier doping induced by gate-controlled intercalation drives a reversible, zero-field antiferromagnetic to ferromagnetic phase transition, enabling direct and full electrical control of both magnetic order and spin polarization.

pmc-12860113.title: Pharmacovigilance and herbal medicines safety: a cross-sectional study of healthcare professionals’ knowledge, attitudes and practices in selected regions of Tanzania, 2021
pmc-12860113.creator: Alambo K Mssusa, Godeliver Kagashe, Sheila Maregesi, Lone Holst
pmc-12860113.description: BackgroundThe World Health Organization recommends integrating the safety monitoring of herbal medicines into existing pharmacovigilance (PV) systems to avoid overburdening the healthcare systems and national PV centres. However, there are few reports (0.3%) of herbal medicine Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs) in the global database originating from Africa.

pmc-12955110.title: Rare localization of a rhabdoid tumor in the elbow of a 6-year-old child: A case report
pmc-12955110.creator: Soukaina Bahha, Nidal Mrani, Asmae Guennouni, Salma EL Aouadi, Zouheir Alami, Tarik el Madhi, Mohamed Khettab, Nabila Louaqad, El Hammany zitouna, Chat Latifa
pmc-12955110.description: We report a rare case of a rhabdoid tumor of the elbow in a 6-year-old child. Rhabdoid tumors are aggressive and rare neoplasms, usually found in the kidneys or soft tissues, and their occurrence in the elbow is exceptional, potentially delaying diagnosis.

pmc-13229922.title: Management of para-aortic paraganglioma in a patient with uncontrolled blood pressure—a case report

This study aimed to assess the seropositivity for Leptospira in patients attending a tertiary care center in Rajasthan and study their clinico-epidemiological profile.

pmc-13560450.title: Integrative evidence-knowledge marker selection enhances LLM-based cell type annotation in single-cell RNA-seq analysis
pmc-13560450.creator: Jiyeong Shin, Soyoung Jeong, Hyun Je Kim, Minsik Oh
pmc-13560450.description: BackgroundCell type annotation is essential for gaining biological insight from single-cell RNA sequencing data, yet manual labeling remains time-consuming and difficult to reproduce. Various computational approaches have been developed to automate this process, and recent studies suggest that large language models can infer cell types with promising accuracy in single-cell analysis.

pmc-13587101.title: SpaHDSRL: hierarchical dual-graph self-supervised representation learning for integrating spatially resolved multi-omics data
pmc-13587101.creator: Xiang Li, Kangkang Zhang, Yifei Li, Fangrong Yan, Bosheng Li, Qian Ding
pmc-13587101.description: Spatial multi-omics technologies facilitate simultaneous measurement of multiple molecular modalities within their native spatial context, offering opportunities to characterize tissue organization and cellular heterogeneity. However, effective integration remains challenging because such data concurrently encode spatial adjacency and molecular similarity, while also being limited by high dimensionality, sparsity, noise, and cross-modality heterogeneity.
